deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (pp. 85-86). This is the end of a numerical procedure, divided into 'Momente', for the secular (mean-anomaly-averaged) part of the attraction of a disturbing planet. That is, it computes the averages of (x'-x)/rho^3, (y'-y)/rho^3 and (z'-z)/rho^3 over the mean anomaly of the disturbing planet, which amounts to the attraction of a 'Gaussian ring'. On p. 85 the constant terms P and Q of (1-(H/F)cos w)^(-3/2) and cos w*(1-(H/F)cos w)^(-3/2) are found with the arithmetic-geometric mean. The 'Fifth Moment' then defines, with t = tan zeta:
- M = t*sqrt(1-t^2)/F^(3/2) * {P cot zeta + P e' cos phi + 1/2 K (P cos k - Q cos(h+k))}
- N cos n = sqrt(1-t^2)/F^(3/2) * {-P t - P e' cos phi t^2 - 1/2 K (P cos k - Q cos(h+k))}
- N sin n = K(1-t^2)/(2F^(3/2)) * {-P sin k - Q sin(h+k)}. The original '+' before Q was deleted; the numbers on this page confirm the minus sign.

THEORY ON THIS PAGE. Write the relative coordinates as functions of the eccentric anomaly E' of the disturbing planet:
- x'-x = A + alpha sin(E'+a)
- y'-y = B + beta sin(E'+b)
- z'-z = C + gamma sin(E'+c)
Average over the mean anomaly, using dM' = (1 - e' cos E') dE'. By linearity:
- <(x'-x)/rho^3> = A*<rho^-3> + alpha*<sin(E'+a) rho^-3>
- [mine] M is the constant part and N sin(.+n-phi) the first-harmonic projection.
Hence the secular parts are AM + alpha N sin(a+n-phi), BM + beta N sin(b+n-phi), CM + gamma N sin(c+n-phi). Here phi is the phase shift between E' and the auxiliary angle w of the earlier reduction.

NUMERICS (logarithms, characteristic -10 understood, 'n' = negative).

(1) Basic quantities.
- log e'cos phi = 8.6341934n and log t = 9.8100541.
- e'cos phi * t = -0.02781298, so log(1 + e'cos phi * t) = 9.9877498.
- log(1-t^2) = 9.7656885, so log sqrt = 9.8828442.
- log F^(3/2) = 1.6520616, so sqrt(1-t^2)/F^(3/2) has log 8.2307826.
- Adding log P = 0.0291619 gives 8.2599445.

(2) The P cot zeta + P e' cos phi part.
- P sqrt/F^(3/2) * (1 + e' cos phi t) has log 8.2476943, i.e. +0.017688634 (first term of M).
- Times t gives log 8.0577484, i.e. -0.011422163 (first term of N cos n).

(3) The P cos k part.
- log(1/2 K cos k) = 9.4790444, so 8.2599445 + 9.4790444 = 7.7389889, i.e. 0.005482629.
- This enters N cos n with a minus sign; times t (log 7.5490430) it gives +0.003540324 in M.
- log(1/2 K sin k) = 7.9162518n. With P and (1-t^2)/F^(3/2) (log 8.1136269) this gives +0.000114562 in N sin n.

(4) The Q part.
- h+k = 178°37'33.62" (it replaces the struck 181°45'39.92"); log cos = 9.9998751n and log sin = 8.3798207.
- log 1/2 KQ = 8.80778..; 1/2 KQ cos(h+k) has log 8.80766..n.
- Times sqrt/F^(3/2) this gives log 7.03845n, i.e. -0.0010926 in N cos n.
- Times t (log 6.84850) it gives +0.0007055 in M.
- 1/2 KQ sin(h+k) has log 7.1876028; times (1-t^2)/F^(3/2) this gives 5.30123, i.e. -0.0000200092 in N sin n.

(5) Sums.
- M = 0.021934453 (log 8.3411268).
- N cos n = -0.017997384 (log 8.2552094n).
- N sin n = 0.0000945528 (log 5.9756744).
- tan n = N sin n / N cos n, so n = 179°41'56.36".
- log cos n = 9.9999940, so log N = 8.2552154.

(6) Angles.
- phi = 206°37'56.50", so n - phi = -26°56'0.14".
- The angles 335°10'11.84", 255°35'19.34" and 16°55'18.81" are a, b, c. [mine, verified]
- Hence a+n-phi = 308°14'11.70" (log sin 9.8951251n), b+n-phi = 228°39'19.20" (9.8754950n), c+n-phi = -10°0'41.33" (9.2401635n; corrects a struck 9.2965151n).
- log alpha = 0.6658677, log beta = 0.6905337, log gamma = 0.4662663.
- So log alpha sin(a+n-phi) = 0.5609926n, log beta sin(b+n-phi) = 0.5660287n, log gamma sin(c+n-phi) = 9.7064298n.

(7) Final.
- log A = 0.4096975, log B = 0.3561942, log C = 8.6131641n.
- AM = +0.05634097, BM = +0.04981051, CM = -0.000900100.
- alpha N sin = -0.06549501, beta N sin = -0.06625888, gamma N sin = -0.009154723.
- Secular parts: X = -0.00915404, Y = -0.01644837, Z = -0.01005482.
errors: No substantive errors; every logarithmic addition I checked agrees to about 1e-7.

Minor last-digit inconsistencies in overwritten figures. From log 7.0384498 one gets 0.00109257 rather than the written 0.001092592. Its product with tan zeta gives about 0.00070551 versus the written 0.000705495. The effect on the result is below 1e-7.

Gauss himself corrected several slips on the page: the value of h+k (181°45'39.92" to 178°37'33.62"), log sin(c+n-phi) (9.2965151n to 9.2401635n), and a struck 7.2453723n. In the formula for N sin n on the previous page the '+' before the Q term was changed to '-'; the numbers here confirm the minus sign.

results.what: The secular (mean-anomaly-averaged) part of (x'-x)/rho^3, with x'-x linear in sin(E'+a), splits as AM + alpha N sin(a+n-phi), using dM' = (1 - e' cos E') dE'.
results.modern_name: Secular perturbations via the averaged attraction of an elliptic ring (Gaussian ring averaging)

results.what: Use of the AGM-computed constants P and Q (complete elliptic integrals) to evaluate the averaged ring attraction numerically.
results.modern_name: Arithmetic-geometric mean evaluation of complete elliptic integrals in secular perturbation theory

results.what: Logarithmic numerical evaluation of M, N, n and of the three secular components for a concrete planetary example.

deep.surprise_reason: The AGM / Gaussian-ring method for secular perturbations is famously Gauss's own (1818). This page is a worked numerical example of an apparently earlier or variant form of it, written in eccentric-anomaly coordinates with an auxiliary angle zeta rather than the published reduction. That is of interest for dating and development, but it is not a new result.

First term of N cos n is approximately 0.011422163 in magnitude.
The P sin k term of N sin n is approximately 0.000114562.

The y-component secular part is approximately -0.01644837.
The z-component secular part is approximately -0.01005482.

transcription_corrections: '- 0,000020092' should read '- 0,0000200092' (one zero is missing; it equals 10^(5.3012297-10)).
'9.9999949' (log cos n) is more likely 9.9999940, since 8.2552094 - 9.9999940 gives the written 8.2552154.
The label '½K cos k sin 7.9162518 n' means log(½K sin k) = 7.9162518n, set beside log(½K cos k) = 9.4790444.
The 'n' after 'sin ... 8.3798207' is doubtful or struck: sin(178°37'33.62") is positive.
The angles 335°10'11.84", 255°35'19.34" and 16°55'18.81" are a, b, c themselves, not a+n-phi; subtracting 26°56'0.14" gives the angles whose sine logs are listed.
'9.4792069' above 8.2599445 in the middle column appears to be a superseded first value of log(½K cos k), replaced by 9.4790444.
The '{+ ... +}' around P cot zeta and -P tan zeta on the previous page marks insertions, not deletions; the numbers here include those terms.
The overwritten digits '8.8076673 n' and '7.0384498 n' may be 8.80766.. and 7.03844.. in their final form; the last digit is uncertain.
